most_likely: Staghorn calculus of right kidney requiring percutaneous nephrolithotomy
summary: Elective urology admission of a man with known bilateral staghorn renal calculi and bilateral percutaneous nephrostomy tubes for definitive stone treatment. He underwent difficult right percutaneous nephrolithotomy for stone >2 cm with antegrade nephrostogram, antegrade ureteroscopy, antegrade ureteral stent placement and removal of the right nephrostomy tube, with residual stone burden requiring interval ureteroscopy. Post-operative course was uncomplicated (POD1 discharge); labs show stable chronic renal impairment (Cr 2.1 → 2.5) and normocytic/macrocytic anemia (Hgb 9.4).

differential.diagnosis: Bilateral staghorn calculi of kidney (right renal calculus treated this stay)
supporting_evidence: Right PCNL for stone greater than 2 cm performed
differential.reasoning: Admission was explicitly for planned stone removal; the renal calculus is the disease driving the entire stay and all procedures.
